what_happened: The job to speed up the slowest test binary, using CI timings supplied to it, failed. The producer made no change to the repo. Its report was sent back once for problems and still did not report four acceptance criteria as met. These were: a CHANGELOG entry listing ten binaries with their "finished in" seconds and the CI run id; a local before and after time for the slowest binary, or a stated reason it cannot be fixed without losing coverage; a diff limited to that binary's tests plus CHANGELOG.md; and a passing run of that binary faster than the "before" time. The job produced no measurements, no fix and no stated reason for the empty run. These were unmet criteria, not failed checks.
cause: Measuring and fixing are still joined in one producer run with one deadline and budget. This is true even though the earlier attempt's lesson was to supply CI timings. The fix depends on a local before-and-after measurement of one binary, and the outcome of that measurement is unknown beforehand. Nothing in the producer stage forces it to write the measurement entry first, to record a partial result, or to give a reason when it stops. The re-send of the report asks for the criteria again, but it does not require a recorded reason for an empty diff. So the run ended with nothing and no diagnosis, as it did last time. Supplying the CI timings removed one long step (the full run) but did not separate the remaining measure step from the fix step.
prevention: Split measure-then-fix jobs into two chained stages, each with its own deadline and budget. Stage one writes only the measurement entry (ten binaries, run id, the slowest binary's local time) and must either commit it or record a stated reason. Stage two reads that entry and makes the fix, or it records the cannot-fix-without-losing-coverage explanation. A producer run that ends with an empty diff must also be required to write a one-line reason (already done, blocked, out of time or gave up) into its report, and the job must fail on that missing reason before the final verdict.
proposed_request: Add the measurement entry for the slowest test binary. Using the CI timings file already supplied (name its CI run id), add one CHANGELOG.md entry that lists the ten test binaries, slowest first, each with its "finished in" seconds. Run only the slowest binary locally with cargo test -p athena-cli --test <binary name> and record its local time in the same entry as the "before" time. Then list the tests inside that binary, slowest first. Change nothing else: no test code, no xtask/shard-timings.txt, no .github/workflows/ci.yml. The entry should describe only the project, with no note about job failures, tooling, access or rerunning. If any number cannot be taken, write the entry with the reason for each missing value instead of leaving it out. A separate follow-up job will fix the single biggest cause in that binary's test code.
